title: Rural Home Loans Late Charge Rule: Grace Period, One Charge per Payment and Waivers
content:
The late charge rule of the Rural Home Loans product.

## Clauses in force

1. **When a late charge arises.** A late charge arises only after more than the product's grace days have passed since the due date of the monthly payment, counted with the due date itself as day 0, so the charge first arises on the day after the last grace day.
2. **One per payment.** Only one late charge may be assessed per monthly payment.
3. **Never netted.** A late charge is never deducted from a later regular payment (which would make that payment late in turn).
4. **Error correction.** A late charge is waived as an error correction when a payment effective on or before the last grace day paid the month in full.
5. **Courtesy.** On request a late charge may be waived as a courtesy only when that month has since been paid in full and the courtesy waivers on the loan in the rolling 12 months are below the product's courtesy waiver allowance. The rolling 12 months run from the same calendar date one year earlier (exclusive) through the day considered (inclusive), and every late-charge waiver granted as a courtesy on the loan in that window counts.

## Retired clauses

- **Retired clause — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis.** "It applies to a monthly payment whose principal-and-interest part is not paid in full by then, at the product's late charge percentage of the scheduled principal-and-interest payment (the monthly principal-and-interest payment), no less than the product's minimum late charge and no more than its maximum late charge, rounded to cents, with the monthly bill as the record it is booked against."
- **Retired clause — no longer in force; superseded by the current basis.** "No late charge is assessed on the escrow part, on a forborne month, or while the loan is in nonaccrual status"

## The grace-period test (clause 1)

- **Clock starts:** the due date of the monthly payment, as shown on that monthly bill in the loan's payment history; that day is day 0.
- **Count:** calendar days, not 24-hour periods.
- **Comparison:** strictly more than the grace days; the last grace day itself is not enough.
- **Evidence:** the system record of the monthly bill against which the charge would be booked, read before the charge is booked.

| Day counted from the due date | Hypothetical product with 15 grace days |
|---|---|
| day 0 (the due date) | no late charge |
| day 15 (the last grace day) | no late charge |
| day 16 (the day after the last grace day) | a late charge can arise |

## Duplicate check (clause 2)

Before a charge is booked, the payment history is read for a late-charge fee already pointing to the same monthly bill; where one exists, no second late charge is assessed for that payment.

## Waiver points of judgement

- A payment effective on the last grace day that paid the month in full: any late charge on that month is waived as an error correction.
- A courtesy waiver is available only on request, only for a month since paid in full, and only while the courtesy waivers in the rolling 12 months are below the allowance. *Hypothetical case:* with an allowance of 1, a loan that already shows one courtesy waiver in the window cannot receive another.
